title: Pici all'Aglione (Tuscan Garlic Pasta)
steps: Dough. Mix semolina and salt, add the water slowly with a fork until crumbly, then squeeze into a rough dough. Knead 2–3 minutes, cover and rest 10 minutes.
Knead again. Knead 2–3 minutes more until elastic, cover and chill 30 minutes.
Shape pici. Roll into a sheet just over ½ cm thick, cut thin strips and roll each between your hands into thick spaghetti. Keep on a semolina-dusted tray.
Confit garlic. Cover peeled garlic with olive oil and cook on medium-low, gently simmering, 20–30 minutes until soft and light golden. Cool, then crush with a pinch of salt into a purée.
Sauce. Heat 4 tbsp of the garlic oil with the purée over medium-high; when it sizzles add the wine and cook off. Add passata and cook 10 minutes until thick.
Finish. Boil the pici in salted water 90 seconds–3 minutes, transfer to the sauce, tear in the basil and loosen with pasta water if needed.
